gen-dafont-nordic-gf-ovo: Nordic cuts its letters like stencils, tight and closed. Ovo, classic and authoritative, has thinner strokes that never turn threadlike, and its open curves let paragraphs of text unfold without strain.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-domine: Domine sets compact ascenders over tall lowercase, dignified and refined. Under the wire-bent lines of Nulshock, those moderate stroke changes and open curves keep long paragraphs moving along smoothly.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-halant: Nulshock stretches wide, its outline steady, arches matching the stems. Halant begins with a faint thick-thin shift and thickens gently at the shoulders, so its towering x-height keeps extended reading sturdy and traditional.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-hedvig-letters-se: Hedvig Letters Serif reads at a steady, sturdy pace with mild contrast. Nulshock glides across the top like wire, and the text serif below lets its open curves take over.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lisu-bosa: Wide and wiry, Nulshock carries each stroke at the same visual weight, with spacious tracking. Lisu Bosa then brings sturdy tall words and gentle weight changes that never turn dramatic, so long reading stays easygoing.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-ovo: Ovo reads with classic authority, tall in the middle band. Hairline-free Nulshock sits on top, and Ovo narrows gradually from stem to terminal, keeping paragraph after paragraph inviting.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-domine: Brushy and blunt, Origami draws one constant stroke, heavy as poured lead type. Domine, a refined serif with modest stroke modulation and breathing room in every curve, makes pages of text feel dignified.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-halant: Chunky and unmistakable, Origami paints one constant stroke. Halant steps in beneath with slight but noticeable stroke contrast and a towering x-height, giving the heading a sturdy, traditional partner.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-hedvig-letters-ser: Origami keeps its bowls as stout as its stems, which is what gives a display line its punch. And Hedvig Letters Serif, with open curves and mild contrast, is the one that handles sustained reading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-montagu-slab: Bent-paperclip strokes give Origami its look, all one constant width. Origami hits hard in display, while Montagu Slab, with its sizable x-height and quiet stroke contrast, handles the actual reading.
